rule: Only URLs actually opened are logged. Printed values that cannot be tied to a dated authoritative dataset are preserved as historical claims and are not used as unqualified current scoring facts.

corrections: Treat the 45-25-25-5 composition as an idealised teaching model, not a fixed composition.
Use pH 7, not 7.2, as neutral under the standard definition.
Treat formation-rate, depth and temperature values as context-dependent rather than universal.
Warn that small-scale maps cannot identify farm-level soil.

The printed nine-order list is incomplete. Current USDA Soil Taxonomy has 12 orders: Alfisols, Andisols, Aridisols, Entisols, Gelisols, Histosols, Inceptisols, Mollisols, Oxisols, Spodosols, Ultisols and Vertisols.
Order definitions must use diagnostic properties; one-line colour or climate shortcuts are memory aids only.
ICAR history identifies J. W. Leather's classical alluvial-black-red-lateritic grouping; avoid attributing the fourfold classification to Voelcker without qualification.
The zonal-interzonal-azonal system is historical and is not equivalent to current Soil Taxonomy.
Keep sheet, rill and gully erosion distinct by channel scale and tillage removability.
Separate agricultural erosion from glacial and coastal geomorphic erosion.
Use current ICAR 2025 national estimates only with source year; retain book estimates as historical.
Explain conservation measures by mechanism and limitations rather than as guaranteed cures.
The 65-25-5-3-1-1 shares are reproduced from the AP Horticulture Vision 2030 profile, but the same document retains Telangana-era regional wording; label the denominator and legacy context.
The book conflicts with itself on laterite and coastal shares across pages 301 and 303; show both printed claims and use the dated source table for scoring.
Current APSAC district soil-resource maps demonstrate mixed soil classes within districts and supersede the book's coarse pre-2022 map for local interpretation.
